On average, human muscle contains approximately equal amounts of Type I

and Type II fibers. However, a large interindividual variability exists with respect to fiber type percentage. The quadriceps of elite sprinters have been shown to have a predominance of Type II fibers, whereas quadriceps of elite aerobic endurance athletes are primarily composed of Type I fibers.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 1: Hypertrophy-Related Responses and Adaptations to Exercise Stress
